The codes associated with my recent papers are not listed below, all the links can be found next to the paper in Publications . Nonlinear Matrix Decomposition s (NMDs) This Matlab code provides the implementation of an ADMM-based algorithm to solve a wide range of NMDs : Given a matrix X(mxn) and a factorization rank r, compute W(mxr) and H(rxn) such that d( X , f (WH) ) is minimized , where d( . , . ) can be the Frobenius norm, the l1 norm or the Kullback-Leibler divergence between X and f(WH), and f( . ) is a function applied component-wise on WH that can be the ReLU function f( . ) = max(0, . ), the square f( . ) = ( . )^2, the MinMax function f( . ) = min(b,max(a, . )), or the absolute value f( . ) = | . |. See A. Awari, N. Gillis, and A. Vandaele, "Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers for Nonlinear Matrix Decompositions" , December 2025. [arXiv] Successive Projection Algorithm (SPA) and its Variants This Matlab code can be used to tackle separable simplex-structured matrix factorization (separable SSMF ): Given a data matrix X = WH+N where H (r-by-n) is column stochastic and contains the r-by-r identity as a submatrix, find an index set K with r indices such that X(:,K)≈ W. It contains the successive projection algorithm (SPA) and 5 variants; see the paper G. Barbarino , N. Gillis, "On the Robustness of the Successive Projection Algorithm" , [arXiv] [code] Or thogonal NMF w ith the Kullback-Leibler divergence This Matlab code contains an alternating optimization strategy for ONMF with the Kullback-Leibler divergence , as well as for the Frobenius norm ; see the paper J.P. Nkurunziza, F. Nahayo, N. Gillis, "Orthogonal Nonnegative Matrix Factorization with the Kullback-Leibler divergence" , October 2024. [arXiv] Non-symmetric semidefinite Procrustes problem This Matlab code contains several algorithms for solving the non-symmetric positive semidefinite (PSD) Procrustes problem: given rectangular matrices X and B, find the matrix A that minimizes the Frobenius norm of AX-B and such that A+A T is PSD. It contains a new semi-analytical approach that is guaranteed to produce an optimal minimum-norm solution. See N. Gillis and S. Sicilia , "Minimum-norm solutions of the non-symmetric semidefinite Procrustes problem" , June 2024. [arXiv] Target Stationary Distribution Problem This Matlab code allows you to solve the Target Stationary Distribution Problem (TSDP): Given an n-by-n stochastic and irreducible matrix G, and a target distribution μ, find a correction matrix Δ such that G+ Δ is stochastic and has μ as its stationary distribution
